title: go-mutants diagnostics bundle manifest v1
description: What one failed run's diagnostics bundle holds, and which failure it explains. The bundle itself is text a person reads; this is the one file in it a program reads, so that a job which uploads the directory can also say what it uploaded without parsing prose. It is an index of a bundle rather than an account of a run: the account is the recording beside it and the claim is the run report, and neither is restated here.

tool_version.description: The build that wrote the bundle. It is the first thing a reader of a bug report needs and the last thing the reporter remembers.

run_id.description: The run this bundle explains. A bundle, a recording and a report of one run all carry it, which is what pairs them afterwards.

platform.description: The machine the run was measured on. Build constraints decide which files a package even has, so a bundle is a statement about one platform.

failure.description: What stopped the run, as the console said it.

code.description: The diagnostic code, when the failure carries one. It is absent rather than empty for an error that does not -- cobra and pflag produce plain errors, and inventing a code for one would be a second identifier for a condition that has none. See docs/errors.md.

summary.description: The first line of the rendered error, which is the line the console printed. The whole of it, the full error and the typed chain underneath are in error.txt.

files.description: Every file the bundle holds, in listing order, each with what it is for. A bundle never writes an empty file, so a name absent here is a question the run had no answer to rather than an answer it left blank -- a run that published no report has no report.json, and a traced run has its stream in this directory already rather than a second copy of it.

preserved.description: The temporary directories the run was asked to keep, in path order, and absent when it kept none. The same paths are in preserved-paths.txt, which is where a person reads them.

name.description: The file's name inside the bundle directory. Never a path: a bundle is one directory deep, so that a reader can list it and a collector can remove it.

holds.description: One line saying what a reader will find in it, so that a bundle attached to a bug report needs no covering note.
